clue.text: Shivering, watch deer in warm clothing

indicators.note: something shivering is shaking and jumbled, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A watcher of deer, out in the cold, is shivering in their warm clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shivering' signals the anagram of WATCH DEER IN; 'in' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A windproof jacket is an outer garment worn to keep warm against cold winds.

clue.text: Comedian always opening with awful gags

indicators.note: the opening of each word is its first letter, taken from these three words

explanation.surface: A comic always starts with terrible jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'always' is only a link word in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A wag is a witty, joking person, so a comedian of sorts.

clue.text: Tearful young woman from Ulster given honour

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster
the OBE is a British honour, Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A weeping girl from Northern Ireland receives an award.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth NIOBE wept endlessly for her slain children and was turned to a weeping stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Niobe of Greek legend is the archetype of the grieving woman forever in tears.

clue.text: Man brought in to teach unusually fast runner

indicators.note: brought in to means placed inside the following letters
unusually means in an unusual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: he is the male pronoun, standing for a man

explanation.surface: A man is hired to teach an exceptionally quick runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teach' reads as the verb in the surface but is only anagram fodder; 'unusually' rearranges it to CETAH before 'brought in to' adds the man.
explanation.definitionFit: This big cat is the fastest land animal, so a fast runner by example.

clue.text: Bound for the ballet

parts.note: reads as heading to the theatre, but means a leap performed in ballet

explanation.definitionFit: This is a jump in ballet during which the dancer crosses the legs rapidly, a bound.

clue.text: Give more drink to whelp

parts.note: to whelp is to give birth to puppies, to pup

explanation.surface: An odd instruction to give extra drink to a puppy.
explanation.definitionFit: To top up a glass is to refill it, giving someone more drink.

clue.text: .Painter seen to chat girl up

parts.note: rap is slang for talk or chat

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Leah is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A painter is seen chatting up a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' looks part of 'chat up' but reverses LEAH to HAEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael was a great Italian Renaissance painter.

clue.text: Gnome used to be retiring

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: used to be is the past tense was

explanation.surface: A garden gnome that once used to be shy and retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnome' is not a garden ornament but its rarer sense: a short pithy saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnome in this sense is a maxim or aphorism, and an old saying is exactly that.

clue.text: Fury that is shown at first — one should clean up

indicators.note: shown at first means this piece goes at the front

parts.note: SC, scilicet, is a Latin abbreviation meaning that is
the Furies of myth were avengers of wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Anger is shown at the start by someone who should be tidying up.
explanation.walkthrough: SC (scilicet, 'namely') is a less common abbreviation for 'that is' than IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scavenger clears up waste or carrion; in old use a street sweeper was given this name.

clue.text: Outlaw, if hit, will crumple, that's for certain

indicators.note: to crumple is to collapse into a disordered heap, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An outlaw who is struck will surely collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will crumple' signals the anagram of OUTLAW IF HIT; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done every time without exception happens for certain.

clue.text: March, seeing simpleton's favourite coming around

parts.note: a goose is a silly person, a simpleton; with the possessive it gives an extra S

indicators.note: coming around means turning about, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Someone watching a march sees a simple person's favourite go by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' is the definition, not the month. 'coming around' is the reversal signal, and 'seeing' is only a link word in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The goose-step is a stiff-legged style of marching, so to do it is to march.

clue.text: Hide incriminating evidence in factory

definitions.meaning: to ... evidence is to hide it secretly so as to incriminate someone

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: planting false evidence, and an industrial plant meaning a manufacturing works.

clue.text: Soldiers infiltrate city and there finally expire

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside, so these letters go into the city's name

parts.note: Bath is an English city in Somerset
RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of soldiers

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Troops infiltrate a city, and there at the end they die.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expire' suggests dying, but here it has its literal sense of breathing out.
explanation.definitionFit: To expire literally means to breathe out, so it is a fair synonym for drawing breath.

clue.text: In disorder, like soldiers returned from leave

definitions.meaning: something the wrong way round is muddled or disordered
soldiers coming back from leave are going back to the front line

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: soldiers returning from leave go back to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means reversed or muddled, and literally describes returning to the front.

clue.text: Put unpleasant smell into ineffective medicine

parts.note: to put something down is to place it
BO, body odour, is an unpleasant smell

explanation.surface: An instruction to add a bad smell to a medicine that does not work anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is a link word here, not a container signal: the pieces simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill given for psychological effect has no active ingredient, so it is medicine with no real effect.

clue.text: Get round

definitions.meaning: to get hold of something, such as a ball
a round is a song sung in canon, and a humorous round is called by this name

explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is not an adverb here but a noun: a type of part-song.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses hold: to grasp or get, and a comic part-song sung as a round.

clue.text: Give way here — twisted joint needs ointment

annotationWithheld.why: Give way here — twisted joint needs ointment (1-8): UNCTION is ointment and 'Give way here' the definition, but no parse of 'twisted joint' gives TJ; the leftover letters do not account for the clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Give way here — twisted joint needs ointment

clue.text: Prince running away in the gloaming

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's name for the young Henry V
flight is the act of fleeing or running away

explanation.surface: A prince flees at dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The gloaming is a poetic word for dusk, when only partial daylight remains.

clue.text: Showing enthusiasm having words with friend

parts.note: the lyric of a song is its words
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone talking with a friend is full of enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' and 'with' are link words joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak or write lyrically is to do it with great enthusiasm or effusiveness.

clue.text: Boastful kind of pigeon

definitions.meaning: one who trumpets their own achievements is boastful
a domestic breed of fancy pigeon bears this name

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is an adjective standing for a noun: a boaster, someone who blows their own trumpet.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who blows their own trumpet is a boaster, and there is also a fancy pigeon breed with this name.

clue.text: Reason for mass list of instructions

parts.note: a pro is an argument or reason for something, as in pros and cons
a gram is a unit of mass

explanation.surface: Someone asks why mass is in a list of instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer program is a coded set of instructions for a machine to follow.

clue.text: Explorer needs a warm coat

parts.note: Mungo Park was a Scottish explorer of the River Niger

explanation.surface: An explorer must have a warm coat for the journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded, padded anorak is a warm winter jacket.

clue.text: Fixes blame on climbing plant

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to pin something is to fix it in place
a rap is blame or punishment, as in take the rap

explanation.surface: Someone pins the blame on a climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing plant' looks like the definition, but 'climbing' turns PINSRAP round; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a plant grown for its pale root vegetable.

clue.text: Confrontation necessitated restart to game?

definitions.meaning: in ice hockey play restarts with the puck dropped between two players

explanation.walkthrough: In ice hockey a face-off starts or restarts play; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a standoff between opponents, and the hockey method of restarting play.

clue.text: Thief has silver wrapped in $5 bill

indicators.note: wrapped in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: fin is US slang for a five-dollar bill
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A thief has some silver tucked inside a five-dollar note.
explanation.walkthrough: FAGIN is the thief who runs a gang of child pickpockets in Dickens's Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's Fagin is a famous fictional fence and thief.

clue.text: Warm drink

definitions.meaning: a warm, friendly welcome is a ... one
a sweet fruit drink or liqueur

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: friendly and warm in manner, and a sweet concentrated fruit drink.

clue.text: 1,000 missing church epic

indicators.note: missing means without, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: a chiliad is a group of a thousand

explanation.surface: A thousand copies of a church epic have gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: CHILIAD is a rare word for a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's Iliad is an ancient Greek epic poem.

clue.text: Specialised dealer in East End branch

indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End drop their aitches, so the initial H goes

parts.note: a hosier is a dealer specialising in stockings and socks

explanation.surface: A trader who specialises in goods sets up a branch in the East End of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'branch' is not a shop branch but a willow twig.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a willow whose pliable branch or twig is used in basketwork.

clue.text: In a tangle working out aspic recipe

indicators.note: working something out involves sorting it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook gets in a muddle trying to work out a recipe with aspic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working out' is the anagram signal for IN A TANGLE, which itself looks like an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A galantine is a dish of boned meat set in aspic jelly, so it is a recipe using aspic.

clue.text: Lug out of the ark

indicators.note: out of means some letters are taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something is lugged out of Noah's ark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lug' is not a verb meaning carry but slang for an ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Lug is an informal word for the organ of hearing.

clue.text: Make black and blue and brown

definitions.meaning: to ... someone's hide is to beat them, leaving bruises

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to thrash someone (tan their hide), and the yellowish-brown colour.

clue.text: It may promise financial gain, or possibly deny promise

indicators.note: possibly suggests another arrangement may be made, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something might promise wealth, or perhaps break its promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals the anagram of DENY PROMISE; folklore says a tiny spider landing on you brings money.
explanation.definitionFit: Superstition holds that this small spider crawling on you is a sign of coming wealth.
